statement: Vegetables are represented by the GAEZ tomato proxy.
Selected crops outside rice, coconuts, maize, vegetables and sugar cane are aggregated as OTH.
Crop-output demand after 2020 grows only with the retained SSP2 population index.
Para rubber has no matching row in any retained low-input GAEZ selection table and therefore contributes only high-input spatial proxy rasters to OTH.
All irrigated crops draw from one pooled agricultural-water commodity.
Direct on-farm liquid fuel is not assigned to individual crop technologies.
unit: PJ direct liquid fuel per crop-technology activity

statement: The v10 energy formulation is inherited as the donor system.
ENV_LAND is enforced in-model in the derived case while ENV_WATER remains reporting-only.
Commodity-result reconciliation accepts the source CSV rounding tolerance.
Land terminal/source closure accepts the source CSV rounding tolerance.
Parallel-stock flow aggregation accepts accumulated source CSV rounding.
The validated v13 BASE TotalCapacityAnnual value that served the 2020 observed activity is transferred once into initial effective capacity.
central_value: active; replace when physical stock and utilization data are assembled
rationale: Moves calibration evidence from an annual activity constraint into an initial stock while retaining time-slice, availability and capacity-to-activity effects already represented by the model.
notes: Sector: End-use sectors without official stock series. Affects: RYT.RC for agriculture heat, industry heat, services heat, navigation, rail and aviation. Replacement evidence: Sector equipment censuses, plant registers, vehicle/vessel/rolling-stock registers and utilization surveys

statement: Positive 2020 effective stocks parsed from the validated v13 CBC results are multiplied by 1.000001 before becoming ResidualCapacity.
rationale: The four-decimal TotalCapacityAnnual CSV truncated the services-heat stock enough to leave a 3.91053e-06 time-slice service shortfall. One part per million is below the source reporting precision, preserves the interpreted stock, and is not an activity constraint.
notes: Sector: Inherited effective end-use stocks. Affects: RYT.RC for stock groups whose physical stock is inherited from the validated v13 solution. Replacement evidence: A lossless full-precision result export or independently observed physical stock and utilization data

statement: The 2020 stock is uniformly distributed over its operational life, producing a linear residual-capacity decline to zero.
rationale: Prevents cliff retirement when asset-vintage microdata are unavailable.
notes: Sector: All recalibrated stocks except power. Affects: RYT.RC 2020-2053. Replacement evidence: Age-cohort or commissioning-year distributions

statement: The base annual adoption allowance is scheduled initial-stock retirement plus the positive increment in service demand converted at the lowest class CapacityToActivityUnit. Each technology's allowance also recursively restores previously allowed new-capacity vintages when they reach that technology's operational life.
rationale: Allows gradual endogenous switching without forcing activity shares and avoids an artificial capacity shortage when endogenous vintages retire later in the horizon.
notes: Sector: Non-road end uses. Affects: Full-horizon RYT.TAMaxCI adoption series for non-road stock-group technologies. Replacement evidence: Annual equipment sales, retirements and utilization surveys

statement: Official 2020 capacity totals scale the inherited v13 residual-capacity trajectories proportionally by technology.
rationale: Corrects the stock total while retaining inherited retirement timing until a unit-level plant register is constructed.
notes: Sector: Power. Affects: RYT.RC for eight existing generation technologies. Replacement evidence: DOE plant-level installed capacity, commissioning, retirement and dependable-capacity register

statement: LPG and kerosene map to COOK_OIL; wood and other map to COOK_BIOM; charcoal maps to the legacy COOK_COAL technology; electricity maps to COOK_ELE.
central_value: active with known charcoal proxy limitation
rationale: Uses every published primary-fuel category while preserving the existing technology and commodity structure.
notes: Sector: Household cooking. Affects: RYT.RC cooking mix. Replacement evidence: A dedicated charcoal commodity/technology and detailed HECS appliance/fuel microdata

statement: Cooking operational lives are 10 years except biomass stoves at 8 years.
rationale: The inherited 15-year life is long for household cooking appliances and no public Philippine survival curve was located.
notes: Sector: Household cooking. Affects: RT.OL, RYT.RC and cooking turnover ceiling. Replacement evidence: HECS appliance ages, sales, retirement or survival data

statement: LTO cars, buses and motorcycles/tricycles map directly; v13 effective light-truck, heavy-truck and van stocks are retained because LTO truck and utility-vehicle categories do not map one-to-one to the model service classes.
rationale: Avoids falsely assigning all utility vehicles to vans or reducing effective freight stock below the service demand implied by the model.
notes: Sector: Road transport. Affects: RYT.RC road fleet. Replacement evidence: LTO body-type/use/fuel microdata reconciled to passenger-km and freight-km classes

statement: The 2020 LTO new-registration count is the annual class market allowance, scaled in later years by the corresponding service-demand index and applied separately to each technology; truck registrations are split by the validated v13 BASE 801:94.8125 light/heavy effective-stock ratio.
rationale: Constrains how quickly any one powertrain can enter without prescribing fuel choice. Because the native constraint is per technology, the sum of all powertrains can exceed the observed class registration total; this is a documented numerical-performance compromise.
notes: Sector: Road transport. Affects: Full-horizon RYT.TAMaxCI adoption series for road stock-group technologies. Replacement evidence: Annual registrations, scrappage, imports, sales and fuel/powertrain shares by model class

statement: Each member technology receives the class annual replacement/registration series as its TotalAnnualMaxCapacityInvestment in every year. The series limits the rate at which any one option can take over, but is not a hard aggregate class-sales cap.
rationale: The local OSeMOSYS NCC1 equation applies the bound directly to NewCapacity without TAL/TAU or fuel/activity shares and without a finite release year. Exact aggregate UDC and permit-network formulations both timed out at 280 seconds, while the no-aggregate optimum showed a 64.25-point maximum annual activity-share change across five classes. Per-technology adoption ceilings reduced that maximum to 37.28 points and eliminated the >25-point cooking and industrial-heat events, but four classes still exceed 25 points because available-stock utilization remains endogenous.
notes: Sector: All recalibrated stock classes. Affects: RYT.TAMaxCI for every recalibrated stock-group member in 2020-2053. Replacement evidence: Technology-specific annual sales, registrations, installations, retirements and market-share data; or an upstream aggregate capacity-investment formulation with demonstrated CBC performance

statement: New capacity investment is zero in 2020 for recalibrated end-use stocks and explicitly listed physical power/fuel-conversion capacities; zero-cost sectoral electricity pass-through technologies remain capacity-free. 2020 is the physical-stock initialization year and endogenous replacement begins in 2021.
rationale: Prevents the optimizer from rewriting physical initial stocks without disabling the model's zero-cost pass-through technologies, which use dummy new capacity rather than residual capacity.
notes: Sector: Recalibrated sectors. Affects: RYT.TAMaxCI 2020 for physical stock technologies only. Replacement evidence: A pre-2020 investment vintage structure or a model horizon beginning after the stock observation date

statement: For 2020-2024, observed renewable dispatch upper bounds are replaced by the same technical activity ceilings used from 2025 onward.
rationale: Removes historical dispatch reproduction while retaining resource availability limits.
notes: Sector: Power. Affects: RYT.TAU for wind, solar, hydro and geothermal. Replacement evidence: Updated renewable resource, hydrology and geothermal production potential studies

statement: The model excludes a national delivered geothermal-heat commodity until a site-specific demand and delivery chain is evidenced; reported small bathing/swimming direct use is not treated as a one-for-one coproduct of electricity generation.
rationale: The inherited branch had no sink or demand and duplicated geothermal electricity activity one-for-one. WGC reports only 0.01265 PJ/year of Philippine direct use in 2019, all bathing/swimming, versus 60.8046 PJ of phantom model heat in 2020.
notes: Sector: Power and direct geothermal use. Affects: Removal of PHL_POW_HEAT, PHL_POW_HEAT1 and the PHL_POW_GEO_OLD heat OAR. Replacement evidence: Site-specific direct-use resource temperature, useful-heat demand, delivery network, efficiency, capacity, utilization and cost data

statement: Use the workbook-v5 recommended PM2.5 technology factors, with EDGAR as a benchmark rather than unquestioned national ground truth.
rationale: The retained v13 record documents the provisional hierarchy and selected values.
notes: Power and navigation remain provisional.

statement: Blue hydrogen captures 70% of the CO2 associated with its natural-gas input.
rationale: Exact implementation and annual values are retained in the calibration record.
notes: A source-specific capture study was not retained.

statement: Represent the Philippines as one national region with shared PHL_WTR_SUR and PHL_WTR_GWT pools; the eight LNDAGRPHLC classes are coefficient classes, not basins or aquifers.
rationale: Matches the actual one-region model topology and avoids inventing absent transfer, basin or aquifer structure.
notes: No local-scarcity claim follows from a national cap.

statement: Use the ERA5 1991-2020 national precipitation climatology as the 2020 normal for rebasing inherited hydrology.
rationale: Provides a current internally consistent 30-year national normal; ERA5 is reanalysis rather than the PAGASA gauge authority.
notes: 2024-2025 provisional annual data are retained only as context.

statement: Install one SSP2-4.5 ensemble-median precipitation pathway as the RCP4.5-equivalent central path.
rationale: SSP2-4.5 shares the 4.5 W/m2 forcing class requested but is not the identical RCP4.5 socioeconomic or model experiment.
notes: The user chooses any additional scenarios; none are preinstalled.

statement: Retain CCKP p10 and p90 values in the evidence snapshot but do not create predefined model scenarios.
rationale: Separates evidence from scenario selection and follows the user's instruction to install only the median.
notes: p10 is drier than the reference in both projection windows, so sign uncertainty remains visible.

statement: Represent 20-year CMIP6 climatologies at midpoint years 2030 and 2050, linearly interpolate annual multipliers, and continue the 2030-2050 slope through 2053.
rationale: OSeMOSYS requires annual values while CCKP publishes period climatologies; the interpolation is transparent and reproducible.
notes: This is a modeling assumption, not an annual forecast.

statement: Apply the combined ERA5 rebase and SSP2-4.5 multiplier to precipitation IAR and surface-water, groundwater and evapotranspiration OARs for all eight coefficient classes and all 30 modes.
central_value: same annual factor on four water ratios
rationale: Preserves each inherited mode's hydrological split and closure ratio while moving the national water envelope with precipitation.
notes: AGRWATPHL irrigation coefficients are not scaled.

statement: Use 125.79 km3/year surface-water potential and 20.2 km3/year groundwater potential as national annual gross-withdrawal sensitivity ceilings.
rationale: These are the available national planning figures and are explicitly labeled potential-flow sensitivities; the PSA abstraction account is retained only to disclose the differing boundary.
notes: They are not dependable yield, environmental-flow-adjusted availability, aquifer stock or safe yield.

statement: Scale both national potential-flow ceilings with the same SSP2-4.5 annual precipitation multiplier used for hydrology.
rationale: Provides a transparent climate-linked national sensitivity in the absence of a calibrated runoff/recharge response model.
notes: This proportional response is an assumption and should be replaced by hydrological modeling when available.

statement: Require DEMAGRGWTPHL to consume one unit of PHL_WTR_GWT for each unit of irrigation-water activity in its single active mode.
rationale: Technology activity and raw-water commodity share the same 10^9 m3 unit; the 1:1 pass-through closes the missing physical link.
notes: Existing pumping-electricity input is retained; pumping energy and lift are not recalibrated.

statement: Put water coefficients and constraint values in SC_0 BASE and preserve null/inheritance rows for COAL_PHASEOUT, RE and EV scenarios.
rationale: Preserves existing scenario semantics and prevents duplicated hard-coded policy data.
notes: All four existing scenarios remain; no water scenario is added.

statement: Do not initialize groundwater storage, head, depletion or aquifer-specific recharge because available evidence does not support those states in this one-region model.
rationale: National potential flow and categorical maps cannot be converted to stored volume or safe yield without aquifer geometry, thickness, storage coefficient, head and discharge data.
notes: The local MUIO formulation fixes StorageLevelYearStart to zero and is not used as groundwater stock.

statement: Use the full-precision post-solve national_water_ledger.json as the authoritative water publication; treat ENV_WATER activity as an unforced zero-cost diagnostic only.
rationale: The existing ENV_WATER terminal is not solver-forced and may take arbitrary cost-degenerate activity.
notes: The ledger reconstructs flows from CBC activities, EBb4 balances, UDC rows and duals.

statement: Represent inherited net crop-water requirements as gross diversions using one national irrigation efficiency.
rationale: The 38 percent observation provides the simplest documented bridge from crop water requirement to gross diversion.
notes: It does not constrain irrigated area or prescribe irrigation uptake.

statement: Represent delivered public-water demand at 70 litres per person per day.
rationale: The single national coefficient keeps demand transparent and population-driven while remaining close to the inherited 2020 public-water scale.
notes: Replace with a documented national delivered-use series when available.

statement: Represent non-revenue water as a constant share of public-water production.
rationale: A single loss factor distinguishes delivered final demand from required utility production without adding a utility submodel.
notes: No source split or utility activity is forced.

statement: Represent national-average groundwater dynamic head for public and power water pumping.
rationale: A single engineering head gives groundwater pumping a physical electricity cost in the one-region model.
notes: Replace with source-specific dynamic heads when available.

statement: Represent combined pump and motor efficiency for public and power groundwater pumping.
rationale: A single engineering efficiency is sufficient for the existing aggregate groundwater routes.
notes: Replace with utility or facility observations when available.

statement: Keep irrigated activity endogenous; represent observed infrastructure only as available initial capacity and never as a demand, lower bound, share or user-defined constraint.
rationale: Food demand and the relative yields costs land availability and water requirements determine whether available irrigation is used.
notes: The older approximately 1.7 Mha benchmark is the FAO 2015 value; the model base-year cross-check is 2.006 Mha in 2020. Alert the user instead of adding a forcing device if a mismatch remains.

statement: Treat the observed 2020 irrigation service area as maintained available capacity through the horizon; use is optional and new expansion remains endogenous.
rationale: The one-region case has no national age distribution with which to construct retirements; constant maintained capacity is the simplest non-forcing stock representation.
notes: Mapped to high-input irrigated rice because the national source does not split irrigation service capacity by model crop and input class; this limitation is disclosed in GAPS.csv.

statement: Treat 2020 rainfed palay harvested area as physical rainfed rice area because one annual rainfed crop is the simplest national interpretation.
rationale: Unlike irrigated rice the national table gives no separate rainfed service area or cropping-intensity series.
notes: This initializes available rainfed capacity and does not require its use.

statement: Calibrate rice OAR as annual production per physical land area; irrigated productivity therefore includes the observed multiple-cropping effect.
rationale: Land activity is annual physical area rather than harvested-event area; irrigated harvested area divided by service area implies about 1.62 crops/year.
notes: Inherited GAEZ cluster ratios are retained by one regime-specific multiplier.

statement: Use the closest national irrigated and non-irrigated palay cost per kilogram as constant real production costs over 2020-2053.
rationale: One observed national cost pair is simpler and more defensible than the inherited token 0.0001 cost.
notes: Future real input-price and productivity paths remain an evidence gap.

statement: Use the DA-PRDP indicative irrigation-system unit cost as the marginal capital cost of endogenous irrigation expansion.
rationale: It replaces an inherited value equivalent to only USD300/ha with a current generic Philippine planning value.
notes: The value is indicative rather than a realized national project-cost average and does not distinguish irrigation technology.

statement: Use a 30-year operational life for endogenous new irrigated-rice capacity.
rationale: A Philippine irrigation appraisal provides a source-backed asset life in place of the inherited generic 15 years.
notes: Applied only to the existing high- and low-input irrigated-rice land options; no capacity or activity is required.

statement: Use 2020 national achieved production per unit of unit-matched area as the absolute crop OutputActivityRatio; do not use absolute GAEZ attainable potential as achieved yield.
rationale: Potential is a ceiling or benchmark and is not an observation of achieved output per land activity.
notes: Applied uniformly across the eight existing clusters because a compatible subnational achieved-yield series is not frozen.

statement: Use irrigation service area for irrigated rice; use harvested/planted area as the available national physical-area proxy for rainfed rice and the retained crop groups.
rationale: This is transparent and unit matched but does not separately identify multiple cropping on annual harvested-area observations.
notes: Observed areas remain benchmark-only; no crop activity equality or share is added.

statement: CRPSGC represents fresh sugar cane and therefore uses fresh-cane tonnes per harvested hectare rather than GAEZ kg sugar per hectare.
rationale: The inherited GAEZ sugar-output coefficient is not dimensionally compatible with the model demand commodity.
notes: No sugar-equivalent commodity or conversion technology is added.

statement: Retain CRPTOM as Other vegetables fresh n.e.c. and CRPOTH as the existing five-component other-crop aggregate; use aggregate-matched production and area rather than a tomato dry-matter proxy.
rationale: Changing the coefficients and descriptions resolves the present unit/definition defect without introducing new model objects.
notes: Composition changes within either aggregate remain outside the current model resolution.

statement: Use the AQUASTAT withdrawal/requirement pairs only as disclosed national boundary benchmarks; do not install either ratio as irrigation efficiency or constrain model withdrawal with them.
rationale: The 2006 Table 4 pair is internally comparable while current variable 4250 is broader than irrigation and neither national aggregate resolves crop scheme season or region.
notes: A compatible efficiency parameter requires crop- or scheme-specific gross diversion and net requirement evidence.

statement: Define CRPCON production and demand as whole coconut with husk; do not interpret or convert it as copra.
rationale: PSA names the observed production product Coconut (w/ husk) and PCA fruit/copra component data confirm a several-fold mass difference.
notes: A future copra use requires a separate commodity conversion technology and sourced process yield rather than silent rescaling.

statement: Interpret the inherited OSeMOSYS Global 01 suffix as investable status and remove the misleading MUIO _T1 resource-tier label.
rationale: The upstream naming specification explicitly defines 01 as investable and does not define wind or solar resource tiers.
notes: Stable TechId values are preserved; no commodity carries _T1.

statement: Represent the single national offshore-wind option with the technical-capacity-weighted net mean of the seven current Philippine offshore development zones.
rationale: The model has one aggregated investable offshore technology rather than a zone or resource-tier supply curve.
notes: The NREL data include 15 percent losses, so wind AvailabilityFactor remains 1 to avoid double derating.

statement: Preserve the inherited 30-timeslice relative offshore-wind shape and scale every nonzero value by one common factor to the sourced annual mean.
rationale: The report establishes annual and seasonal behavior but the exact hourly zone files were not frozen into this build; uniform scaling preserves the existing adequacy shape without fabricating hourly observations.
notes: A future hourly rebuild is recorded as a gap.

statement: Restore the inherited engineering availability factor of 0.9 for the existing geothermal technology; use observed 2020 utilization only as a validation benchmark.
rationale: Availability 1.0 incorrectly assumes no planned or forced outage; directly fitting the 2020 utilization outcome would conceal dispatch, steam-field and outage drivers.
notes: The existing 4 GW capacity ceiling remains unchanged and limits annual output to 113.5296 PJ at 0.9 availability.

statement: Use the NREL/USAID restricted land-use screen as the continuing national onshore-wind technical resource ceiling.
rationale: The stricter screen excludes land that is not realistically available and replaces an unsupported 1594.08 PJ ceiling.
notes: This is an upper resource limit, not an observed generation target.

statement: Use FAO's conservative heavy well-puddled clay values where cluster paddy-soil measurements are absent: 200 mm saturation 2 mm/day percolation for 100 days and 50 mm standing water.
rationale: This is the documented lower engineering case and avoids selecting a sandy high-loss value without cluster soil evidence.
notes: Cluster soil measurements are a high-priority gap.

statement: Hold the observed 2020 national irrigated-palay harvested-area to physical-service-area ratio constant when annualizing the rice water coefficient.
rationale: The model's land activity is physical service area while the calibrated annual crop OAR already embodies multiple cropping.
notes: Does not impose annual activity or harvested area.

statement: Do not calibrate rice IAR by scaling to a national irrigation or agricultural withdrawal total.
rationale: Crop and cluster coefficients must preserve physical engineering meaning; national totals remain validation benchmarks.
notes: Consistent with the non-forcing calibration rule.

statement: Represent gross irrigation diversion at AGRWATPHL without adding an unsupported structural allocation of seepage drainage conveyance loss and recoverable return flow.
rationale: The requested repair is data-only and no source supports a cluster-specific return-flow partition.
notes: Return-flow structure is retained as a disclosed gap.

statement: Exclude PSA/NAMRIA Sea and ocean from the terrestrial model and reconcile the remaining land pro rata to the inherited 295813.1 km2 geographic control.
rationale: Preserves the current model geography and closes the land account without adding or dropping modeled territory.
notes: The pre-reconciliation difference is disclosed in the input snapshot.

statement: Map brush/shrubs to grassland/woodland, marsh/swamp to water bodies, and fishpond to other agricultural land.
rationale: Matches the available model stocks while preserving the official forest boundary and treating fishpond as managed production land.
notes: Replace if a future model adds wetland or aquaculture-land stocks.

statement: Initialize all eight national ENV_LAND modes with lower-equals-upper activity bounds in 2020 and keep MINLNDTOT lower-equals-upper at 295.8131 thousand km2 in every model year.
rationale: A forest floor absorbs the rewarded residual and an open national endowment lets area disappear; equality fixes the observed base year and closes every annual national account.
notes: National totals only; no unsupported per-cluster pro-rata pins.

statement: Reuse existing LNDOTHTOT mode 2 as a nonnegative endogenous idle/fallow cropland route, capped at its observed 2020 balancing stock, rather than adding a new technology or global mode.
rationale: Separates observed cropland cover from productive harvested-area-equivalent activity while preventing an accounting mode from absorbing brush as unsourced new idle cropland.
notes: 2020 solved idle/fallow is 5.2877 thousand km2; productive crop technologies have no added upper bound.

statement: Both LNDOTHTOT modes produce LOTHTOT, so idle/fallow cropland inherits the existing cluster mode-29 other-land hydrology coefficients.
rationale: Preserves the existing water links without inventing national-to-cluster land-cover shares.
notes: Upgrade with measured idle/fallow evapotranspiration/runoff and spatial allocation.

statement: Retain forest mode-27 VC=-10 while adding a national expansion envelope; defer restoration/conversion costs or lags and benefit sensitivities.
rationale: Preserves the user's forest-benefit policy signal while separate activity bounds prevent implausible instantaneous expansion.
notes: Future cases proposed: 0, -5, -10, and a higher-benefit case.

statement: Use the original National Greening Program target area divided by its six-year period as a conservative national forest-expansion envelope rate.
rationale: Provides a transparent Philippine policy-scale rate and prevents the rewarded forest mode from taking the entire residual in one year.
notes: Programme target area is not measured net forest-cover change; the model uses it only as an upper-envelope proxy.

statement: Preserve the reconciled true-grassland component and apply the DENR/MPFD 80 percent production-plantation suitability screen only to the mapped brush/shrub component when limiting net forest expansion.
rationale: The national DENR/MPFD screen supplies a documented central suitability fraction while excluding true grassland from forest conversion.
notes: The ceiling is forest-only. Cropland and built-up land may use the full mapped brush stock. Upgrade with a current parcel overlay of legal forestland, tenure, slope, soils, biodiversity and restoration suitability.

statement: Grow built-up land in proportion to the model's PSA Scenario 2 population and a linearly rising urban share from 54 percent in 2020 to 65 percent in 2050, holding the share constant thereafter.
rationale: Population alone misses continuing urbanization; constant built-up area per urban resident is a transparent aggregate central approximation.
notes: No density sensitivity or spatial allocation is included. Development draws land through the closed national balance.

statement: Keep other agricultural land (mapped fishpond), barren land and water bodies equal to their reconciled 2020 stocks in every future year.
rationale: The aggregate model lacks sourced fishpond, barren-land and wetland transition trajectories; allowing these stocks to disappear created physically invalid residual adjustments.
notes: Built-up land is no longer fixed; it follows ASM_PHL_V17_BUILT_UP_CENTRAL_PATH.

statement: Keep total cropland at least at its reconciled 2020 stock while allowing productive crop area to respond endogenously to crop demand and retaining the balance as idle/fallow mode 2.
rationale: Prevents the model from treating observed idle/fallow cropland as immediately disposable while preserving endogenous food-production choices.
notes: This is a land reserve, not a forced production level; modeled crop demands remain unchanged.

statement: Use 0.70 as the interim central geothermal annual availability ceiling.
rationale: The v16 installed and dependable benchmarks support a physical ceiling well below 0.90 while 0.70 avoids fitting utilization as a target.
notes: Replace with plant-level outage and steam-field availability data.

statement: Use source-year USD values directly because the inherited model declares no common price year.
rationale: This is more transparent than falsely labelling mixed-year evidence as constant 2020 USD.
notes: A common real price year remains a high-priority gap.

statement: Hold the selected coal and SMR capital-cost benchmarks flat through 2053.
rationale: Installs central evidence without adding an unsupported learning or escalation forecast.
notes: Source reference years differ and are explicit.

statement: After observed 2024 production apply a 0.8 percent annual decline to the domestic-route ceiling.
rationale: Transparent interim continuation compatible with the DOE PEP decline narrative while retaining possible supplementary domestic fields.
notes: Not a field-reservoir forecast; update when the Malampaya Phase 4 production profile is public.

statement: Use the DOE-reported combined 8 MTPA operating-terminal capacity as the import ceiling from 2024.
rationale: A physical receiving ceiling is preferable to unconstrained import activity and does not force use.
notes: Does not include later proposed terminals or the PEP 2050 additional-capacity option.

statement: Treat approximately 22.1 GJ/t as a conversion check only until the exact DOE table is retained.
rationale: Prevents the 17.6 GJ/t Indonesian-coal proxy from being silently used for Philippine price conversion without overstating evidence precision.
notes: No v18 coal-price model cell changes.

statement: The inherited coal, gas, oil and biomass CHP _OLD technologies receive zero new-capacity entry throughout 2020-2053; their unchanged 2020 residual-capacity stocks remain available until retirement.
rationale: These are inherited-stock representations, not investable technology options; geothermal remains the documented exception because the model has no separate geothermal new-build or repowering technology.
notes: classification=technology-role rule; no residual-capacity value changes

statement: Only allowances established from 2026 onward are recycled at operational life; unbounded pre-2026 defaults are not interpreted as physical permitted capacity.
rationale: The deployment envelope starts in 2026 while every source cell through 2025 is preserved; recycling 9999/999999 defaults would defeat the physical bound.
notes: classification=judgmental implementation boundary following the v14 allowance-recycling method

statement: Every unit of fixed national land is routed through exactly one of the eight existing hydrological coefficient clusters in every year.
rationale: The clusters partition national geography and their existing TAUs sum exactly to the fixed national land total; bypassing them suppresses rainfall over unused land.
notes: Continuing physical identity, not a historical land-cover or crop-activity target.

statement: The existing 0.38 national efficiency converts gross surface/groundwater withdrawals to water delivered at the cluster field boundary.
rationale: Places gross diversion and delivered crop-water coefficients on a consistent boundary while retaining gross withdrawal activity.
notes: The 62 percent loss destination is outside the current model boundary and remains a disclosed gap.

statement: For each cluster mode and year, preserve the inherited groundwater share of non-evapotranspiration excess water when closing the water balance.
rationale: Corrects conservation without inventing a new groundwater/surface partition or fitting a national outcome.
notes: Upgrade when cluster-specific runoff and recharge evidence becomes available.

statement: Each cluster mode conserves precipitation plus delivered irrigation as evapotranspiration, groundwater recharge and surface runoff.
rationale: A physical commodity-conversion identity prevents mode-dependent creation or loss of water inside land hydrology.
notes: No basin routing, storage, return-flow partition or crop-location shares are added.

statement: In the RE clean-energy scenario, conventional nuclear may commission from 2032 at the existing 1.20 GW/year v18 nuclear expansion rate.
rationale: PEP places first commercial nuclear operation and at least 1,200 MW in 2032. The scenario-specific start year is moved to 2032 while retaining the already documented v18 conventional-nuclear annual ceiling.
notes: classification=policy-scenario commissioning envelope; upper bound only; the existing aggregate PEP milestone remains separate

statement: In the RE clean-energy scenario, nuclear SMRs may commission from 2032 at the existing early-market 0.30 GW/year v18 SMR expansion rate.
rationale: PEP discusses SMRs as a potentially faster-deployment nuclear option and does not prescribe the technology mix. The RE entry year moves to 2032 while retaining the documented v18 SMR rate.
notes: classification=policy-scenario commissioning envelope; upper bound only; no SMR minimum or technology share

statement: From 2035 onward the RE scenario inherits the policy-neutral SC_0 nuclear commissioning ceilings instead of overriding conventional nuclear with zero.
rationale: The PEP clean-energy scenario includes nuclear; retaining a zero conventional-nuclear override conflicts with that scenario. Sparse inheritance keeps physical deployment rates consistent across scenarios.
notes: classification=scenario-overlay correction; SC_0 remains unchanged

statement: Power-sector initialization uses only the fleet operating in 2020; observed 2021-2025 additions are validation benchmarks, not initial stock or forced investment.
rationale: All sectors should remain endogenous after the common 2020 start year; reproducing later additions with equal lower and upper bounds violates the non-forcing rule.
notes: RC remains unchanged; later observations are retained in the validation artifact.

statement: The aggregate DOE register of projects classified as committed at end-2020 is not translated into technology-year minimum investment because a lossless project-to-model mapping and irreversible construction screen were not established.
rationale: Aggregate MW by plant type does not prove model technology, commercial-operation year, surviving status or irrevocability for each project.
notes: A future project-level register may support minimums only for demonstrably irreversible commitments known in 2020.

statement: Mature investable power technologies are allowed to enter endogenously from 2020 unless a continuing physical deployment envelope applies.
rationale: The first model year is not a historical activity-reproduction window; capacity choice remains endogenous after the 2020 stock is initialized through RC.
notes: Applies to onshore wind, solar PV, NGCC, large hydro and geothermal in 2020; existing 2026+ envelopes remain.

statement: PHL_POW_PP_COAL may commission at most 2.0 GW/year during 2020-2029; later 2.5, 3.0 and 5.0 GW/year bands are retained unchanged.
rationale: A deliberately generous continuing construction, finance, permitting and grid-integration envelope; it limits speed but does not require coal investment or dispatch.
notes: Judgmental physical envelope extended to the full first decade; CoalPhaseOut retains exact zero from 2031.

statement: In MUIO scenario inheritance, JSON null means inherit while numeric zero is an active exact bound; CoalPhaseOut therefore uses 0, not 0.0001, from 2031.
rationale: The generator tests for null/None before applying active scenarios, so replacing zero with a small positive value would incorrectly permit capacity.
notes: The scenario overlay itself is unchanged; generated TOMORROWLAND values verify the exact zero.

statement: Border prices are exogenous economic drivers; observed extraction, import, export and source-share quantities remain validation benchmarks and are not activity constraints.
rationale: The model should choose domestic use, import and export routes endogenously from physical envelopes and consistent economic drivers.
notes: No TAL, TAU, share, equality or calibration window is added by this correction.

statement: Coal customs unit values are converted with 22.1 GJ per tonne, the retained Philippine coal energy-content basis.
rationale: Provides one explicit energy normalization for CIF and FOB customs values.
notes: Grade-specific calorific values remain unavailable and are recorded as a gap.

statement: Crude values are converted with 6.119 GJ/barrel and 158.987294928 litres/barrel.
rationale: Converts DOE million-litre volumes and Galoc USD/barrel prices to the model's MUSD/PJ convention.
notes: MUSD/PJ is numerically equal to USD/GJ.

statement: The existing single coal pool and single crude pool treat domestic and imported energy as interchangeable after source tagging.
rationale: No grade, port, plant-specification or refinery-compatibility substructure is added in this minimal price correction.
notes: This causes zero modeled exports under corrected price parity and is disclosed rather than hidden with pins.

statement: PHL_POW_PP_SPV may commission at most 4.0 GW/year during every year from 2020 through 2029.
rationale: Extends the existing judgmental, policy-neutral 2026-2029 construction/financing/permitting/grid envelope across the full decade for temporal consistency.
notes: classification=judgmental; not an observed-capacity calibration forecast or target; should be sensitivity-tested

statement: The established 2026-2029 maximum-investment bands for PHL_POW_PP_WON, PHL_POW_PP_SPV, PHL_POW_PP_COAL, PHL_POW_PP_COAL_CCS, PHL_POW_PP_NGCC, PHL_POW_PP_NGCC_CCS, PHL_POW_GEO_OLD, PHL_POW_PP_HY_LA, PHL_POW_PP_BIOM_CCS and PHL_POW_PP_H2 apply throughout 2020-2029.
rationale: Extends the existing judgmental physical envelopes backward for temporal consistency and closes open/default early-year values.
notes: Not a forecast target or historical calibration; later bands and unlisted technologies remain unchanged.

statement: Offshore wind, SMR and conventional nuclear remain unavailable until their specified entry dates; PHL_POW_GEO_OLD receives annual expansion headroom plus scheduled residual retirement; inherited _OLD fossil and biomass technologies receive zero expansion.
rationale: Represents industry-readiness timing and permits replacement of retiring geothermal stock without forcing it.
notes: Geothermal greenfield and repowering share the existing cost efficiency availability and lifetime representation.
